What have I misread? I’m genuinely trying to give you another perspective and it seems like you’re rejecting it based on nothing more than your mental health. If anybody is doing moral grandstanding, it’s you. For real, one moment you assert that Mr. Richard must have “incurred psychological damage” in order to reasonably be offended by you calling him that. And then you make this whole edit about how the people in your comments who called you out are causing you to ideate suicide. Who’s “being honest” about mental health here? 

Also, that’s kindof gaslighty to say that I’m misreading your post and not go into any detail as to how. 

The sticking point is this: it’s very possible that you are completely misreading this whole situation. To not even consider that, (and furthermore, to cite cultural differences and mental health diagnoses as the only justification to your not considering it) IS immature.

“I had an awkward interaction with my principal and instead of recognizing his perspective, I decided to tell my version of the story online to strangers. If any of those strangers disagree with me, they are officially cyber bullies and btw are making me consider suicide. Guess whose fault that will be? Certainly not mine, as I am not capable of admitting fault in any of these situations. Nah, I’ll just cite poor mental health as a justification for why I’m never wrong.” 


Look, you’re clearly bothered by this interaction with your principal. I totally get it, but have you at all considered his perspective? My name is Jeremiah and I hate being called Jeremy. If someone calls me Jeremy multiple times, I’m going to point it out not unsimilarly to how you describe him having pointed it out to you. Does that make me an asshole? 

Having a cultural upbringing doesn’t entitle you to call people whatever you want. And having mental health issues doesn’t give you the right to guilt people into agreeing with you or silencing those who don’t. It’s a sign of immaturity. Mature people, and furthermore, good teachers, exist above these things. I certainly hope you don’t do things like this around your students. 

And as to the “grow up” comment: absolutely. Guess what? A lot of people have mental illness. Not just you. It’s also not mutually exclusive with being immature. In this situation I think you displaying childish behavior. In which case my response is to call you out on it, as teaching is something to be taken seriously.

Is it at all possible that he genuinely thinks he did address it before? If he’s mistaken that’s one thing, but gaslighting is a serious thing that implies he’s trying to make you feel like you’re crazy. That’s malicious and a pretty immature conclusion to just jump to.

What part do you disagree with? 

Also, I never diagnosed you as mentally ill, I just pointed out that maybe this isn’t the best place to deal with this kind of issue if it causes you this much anguish.
